verdict.rationale: Lithic's Authorization Rules Engine, ASA webhooks, and Events/webhooks API are genuinely autonomous background systems that evaluate every transaction and fire without human intervention, and the MCP server blog post explicitly frames this as AI agents configuring/adjusting these controls autonomously ('eliminating reliance on developer teams'). However, evidence stops at 'AI configures the rule via natural language'; there's no shown mechanism for scheduled/triggered agent-initiated automations beyond the rules engine itself, and no independent/hands-on report of an agent running unattended in production over time. Missing for 10: evidence of agent-initiated scheduled/triggered jobs distinct from the rules engine, and independent corroboration of long-running autonomous agent operation.
